newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah well supported in late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah well supported in late trading.

text.p: Indonesia's rupiah stabilised against the dollar in slow late trading on Tuesday, with swap rates seen recovering on profit-taking, dealers said.
One local bank dealer said spot dollar was capped at the 2,350.0 level despite repeated attempts to breach the barrier.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,348.60/49.10 at 0925 GMT compared with an opening of 2,348.30/49.30.
The dealer said spot rupiah seemed to have recovered from the day's low of 2,350.25 but the underlying tone remained biddish for the dollar due to sustained ample rupiah supply.
Overnight money fell to nine percent from 12.0 percent.
The dealer said operators tended to stay short on the swap market but they were reluctant to be really aggressive because of a possible turnaround in the liquidity condition.
Overnight swap was at 0.15/0.25 and tom/next at 0.30/0.45.
One European bank dealer said operators who went short on Monday had taken profit because of the cheap swap rates.
"Swap rates at 8.0 percent were too cheap. People would naturally cover at this current level," one swap dealer said.
Dealers said the relatively low swap rates, with roll-over costs at around 30 cents, encouraged players to go short in the market.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,349.10/49.45 and 2,349.0/49.5, respectively.
Dealers said the overnight dollar deposit rate was still a bit high but was on the way to stabilise at its previous level of around 5.5 percent. It was last quoted at 5.75/6.0 percent.
One-month swap fell to 15.5/16.5 from 15.0/16.0, two to 30.0/31.5 from 29.25/30.50, three to 47.0/48.3 from 47.0/48.0 and six to 97.0/99.0 from 97.5/98.0 points.
The central bank kept its intervention rate at 2,344/2,462 and the conversion rate at 2,344.0/2,390.0 on Tuesday.
